scope: Single-run Operations / Atelier Dawn screenshot in both A/B arms; original-observer is the separate original S1 invocation sequence.
interpretation: A-06 first hit the result deadline while awaiting navigation-load. It did not get a Browser.close acknowledgement; close processing and OS exit later also missed the remaining budget and triggered owned termination.

The original-observer sequence finished three invocations and failed the fourth first at result/navigation-load. Its fourth invocation subsequently acknowledged Browser.close and closed the WebSocket, but the kernel still showed the root alive at the deadline. This is distinct from the earlier archived post-result exit failures.

All B invocations observed the exact owned target destruction after its close acknowledgement and before sending Browser.close, passed the original Operations screenshot assertions, and exited naturally under the unchanged budget.

This limited A/B sample observed no recurrence of the historical pattern of a verified result followed by acknowledged close and a live root at the deadline in either arm. The observed B behavior supports the barrier as a viable sequencing change. It does not identify the exit failure root cause or establish that the barrier fixes its incidence.
